title: Venezuela Frees Political Prisoners After Leader Meets Trump
summary:
In the early hours of Saturday morning, several political prisoners walked out of detention centers in Venezuela. A political prisoner is someone jailed for their beliefs or their opposition to the government, not for a regular crime. Rights group Foro Penal says "a significant number" were freed.

One of them was Wilder Vasquez. He was given a five-year sentence back in 2018 over claims he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro. Another was Miguel Castillo Cedeño, who rights groups say had been held since June 2019.

The releases came just days after Venezuela's interim leader, Delcy Rodríguez, met U.S. President Donald Trump at the United Nations in New York on Tuesday. Trump captured Maduro earlier this year. Rodríguez's government had already released hundreds of prisoners as part of a reconciliation effort, but that slowed down in April when she said the program was "coming to an end."

Venezuela's government hasn't said whether the new releases are connected to the meeting. It also continues to deny that it jails dissidents, calling the releases a gesture of goodwill. Opposition and human rights groups say Maduro's government used these detentions for years to silence critics. Now they're renewing calls for free elections — something the U.S. has supported in the past.
why_it_matters: It shows that decisions made by leaders far away can change real people's lives — and that pressure from other countries can help free people who were jailed for speaking up.

background_read: Venezuela (a country on the northern coast of South America) was led for years by Nicolás Maduro, whose government the United States has long opposed.
The United Nations (a group where almost all countries meet to talk about big world problems) is in New York City, and world leaders often travel there to meet each other.
Foro Penal (a Venezuelan human rights group) keeps track of people it believes are locked up for their political beliefs rather than for real crimes.
Article_Structure: WHO: Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodríguez, U.S. President Donald Trump, and freed prisoners including Wilder Vasquez and Miguel Castillo Cedeño.
WHAT: Several political prisoners walked out of detention centers just days after Rodríguez met Trump at the United Nations.
WHERE: In Venezuela, with the meeting taking place at the United Nations in New York.
WHY: Rights groups say Maduro's government jailed critics for years to silence them and want free elections, while the government calls the releases a gesture of goodwill.

perspectives.description: Families and rights groups see the releases as a good sign: people who spent years in jail are finally walking free, and the meeting with Trump may have pushed it along.
Human rights groups warn that only some prisoners were freed and the government still denies jailing people for their beliefs, so the bigger problem is not solved.
The government says the releases are goodwill and are not tied to the meeting, and nobody has proof that a deal was made.
